name: security-github-actions-cache-trust-review
intent: GitHub Actions cache producer identity and privileged consumption
artifacts: Cache keys/restore prefixes, branch/event scoping, producer permissions and trusted consuming job.
trace: Follow a lower-trust producer artifact into a privileged job that treats restored bytes as code or authoritative metadata.
experiment: Use a local cache model or isolated repository with inert markers; compare the intended cache producer with a permitted lower-trust key/restore context.
disproof: A broad restore prefix is not cache poisoning without a producer path and security-relevant consumer.
repair: Bind cache trust to producer/context or validate consumed artifacts, preserving legitimate safe reuse.
branch_decisions: Apply GitHub cache ref visibility before modeling a poisoned key: a cache created for a pull-request merge ref is not automatically restorable by main under the same key. Trace default-branch visibility, restore-prefix selection and the privileged consumer. If platform scope prevents restoration, the proposed cross-ref chain fails at that edge.
